title: Los Angeles weather: Rain returns to Southern California as large waves continue to batter coast. Here's what to expect - ABC7 Los Angeles
text:
Los Angeles weather: Rain returning to Southern California as large waves continue to batter coast - ABC7 Los Angeles 
 24/7 Live Los Angeles Orange County Inland Empire Ventura County California Weather 
 High surf continues as another storm set to bring more rain to SoCal 
 Southern California is expected to see a break in wet weather Tuesday before another storm brings renewed chances of rain later this week. Tuesday, November 17, 2026 4:01AM Share Follow ABC7 on Google Este artículo se ofrece en Español LOS ANGELES (KABC) -- Southern California is expected to see a break in wet weather Tuesday before another storm brings renewed chances of rain later this week, including the potential for heavier rainfall.
 Tuesday is expected to be dry with mild temperatures across much of the region. Some areas will see partly cloudy skies.
 Another storm is expected to arrive Wednesday night and continue into Thursday. Some areas could receive between 1 and 3 inches of rain.
 Current estimates indicate heavier rain could reach Los Angeles County during the Thursday morning rush hour, potentially affecting commuters. ABC7 has issued a Weather Change Alert for Thursday because of the anticipated rainfall. Showers could linger into Friday.
 Meanwhile, high surf advisories remain in effect along beaches in Ventura, Los Angeles and Orange counties. According to the National Weather Service, Ventura County beaches could see waves of 7 to 10 feet, Los Angeles County beaches could see waves of 5 to 8 feet, and west-facing beaches in Orange County could experience waves of 6 to 10 feet.
 Officials advised residents and visitors to stay out of the water because of dangerous conditions.
 Tuesday forecast
 Los Angeles and Orange counties Tuesday can expect partly cloudy conditions, along with a high of 65 and a low of 48.
 The valleys and Inland Empire Tuesday will see partly cloudy conditions, with a high of 66 degrees and a low of 45.
 Beach communities can expect partly sunny conditions, with a high of 68 and a low of 52 on Tuesday. Elevated surf and dangerous rip currents will continue along the coast.
 Mountain communities will be mostly sunny Tuesday, with a high of 41 degrees and a chilly overnight low of 18.
 Desert areas can expect a high of 57 and a low of 27 on Tuesday. Palm Springs will see a high of 70.
